superpowers.note: Verified claims hold (m=mouse toggle, Ctrl+c then is_help_toggle order, Backspace/nav_history, into_offset_iter loop) and it catches the nested-list flush stamping pitfall, corrupt-file never-overwrite, and text-fingerprint relocation across edits.

code-design.note: Clean units and numbered call chains with error paths (accepts_text_input reuse, ~51 Line literal sites all check out), but stamping by range.start at flush time mislabels parent list text before a nested list and the stored row offset is fragile across resize.

plain.note: Accurate current-state section and sound anchor/resolve design, but viewer integration is prose-only with no signatures or call chains, and slide-mode support and corrupt-file overwrite behavior are underspecified.

feature-dev.note: Accurate line references (2528, 935, 1647) and covers live-reload remap, margin glyph and nav_history, but stores line numbers only so offline edits drift, and scope creep (four new modules, resize-anchored rebuild, NavEntry refactor) makes it heavy to review.

reason: W combines verified codebase claims with the most complete failure-path coverage (nested-list stamping, never-overwrite on corrupt store, text-based relocation after edits, pending key before help toggle) in a tight design a reviewer can challenge unit by unit. Z and X are solid but respectively over-scoped with line-only anchors and flawed on flush-time stamping, while Y is correct but too thin on viewer-level design to review.
